**About 12.8% of Alberta children under 18 were in poverty in 2024**, the latest year available. The measure is the Market Basket Measure (2023 base), which is Canada's official poverty line.

- **Source:** Statistics Canada, table 11-10-0135-01, vector v1792632015. The series is Alberta, persons under 18, Market Basket Measure (2023 base), percentage of persons in low income.
- **Reference period:** 2024, released 2026-04-29.
- **Recent trend:** 11.9% in 2023, 12.0% in 2022, 8.1% in 2021 and 4.6% in 2020.
- **Other measures:** The same table has other low-income lines, such as the after-tax Low Income Measure, which would give different rates. I didn't pull those.

The average total income in Alberta was **$66,100** in 2024. That is the latest year available. The figure is in 2024 constant dollars and covers people aged 15 and over with income, excluding zeros. It is before tax.

- **Source:** Statistics Canada, Table 11-10-0239-01, Income of individuals by age group, gender and income source.
- **Series:** v107680657 (Alberta; 15 years and over; total gender; total income; average income, excluding zeros). Annual.
- **Recent years:** 2023 was $66,300 and 2022 was $66,000, in the same constant dollars.
- **Caveat:** StatCan marks this table as archived, so it may no longer be updated.
- **Not covered:** This is average income per person. Household or family income, and the median, are different figures.

Alberta's median total income was **$96,600** in 2024. That is before tax and after government transfers, in current dollars.

- **After-tax:** the median was $85,300 for the same year.
- **Source:** Statistics Canada, table 11-10-0237-01 (Canadian Income Survey), reference period 2024, released 2026-04-29. The two figures are from the coordinates 12.2.1.20 (total income) and 12.3.1.20 (after-tax income).
- **Vector IDs:** I didn't retrieve them, so I can't cite them.
- **Not strictly households:** the table counts "economic families and persons not in an economic family". That is the closest match to households in this table, but it isn't the same unit.
- **Recent trend:** the 2023 total-income median was $98,400, so the 2024 figure is lower. Statistics Canada revised the 2018–2023 estimates when the 2024 data came out.
